title: Melde fravær på jobb — tell work you cannot attend
goal: State that you cannot attend work, give the relevant timing, and state the next contact or handover.

objectives.statement: State that you cannot attend work, give the relevant timing, and state the next contact or handover.

spans.value: Before the workday
It is 7:15 on Tuesday morning. Sara is supposed to start work at eight and lead a customer meeting at ten. She has become ill during the night, so she calls her team leader, Henrik.
Hei, Henrik. Det er Sara. Jeg er dessverre syk og kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

blocks.translation: Hi, Henrik. It’s Sara. Unfortunately, I’m ill and can’t come to work today.

spans.value: Det var leit å høre. Vet du om du blir borte hele dagen?

blocks.translation: I’m sorry to hear that. Do you know whether you’ll be away all day?

spans.value: Ja, jeg blir hjemme hele dagen. Jeg gir deg beskjed innen klokka tre om jeg kan komme på jobb i morgen.

blocks.translation: Yes, I’ll stay home all day. I’ll let you know by three o’clock whether I can come to work tomorrow.

spans.value: Greit. Hva gjør vi med kundemøtet klokka ti?

blocks.translation: All right. What do we do about the customer meeting at ten?

spans.value: Jeg har sendt notatene til Nora, så hun kan ta møtet.

blocks.translation: I’ve sent the notes to Nora, so she can take the meeting.

spans.value: Flott. Takk for at du sier fra. God bedring!

blocks.translation: Great. Thanks for letting me know. Get well soon!

spans.value: Takk. Jeg kontakter deg i ettermiddag.

blocks.translation: Thanks. I’ll contact you this afternoon.

spans.value: Sara’s call is short, but Henrik receives all the information he needs. She says that she cannot attend work, gives the relevant timing, and explains what will happen next. She also deals with one urgent task by handing it over to Nora.
A useful workplace absence message has three parts:

items.value: Say that you cannot attend work.
Say when you will be absent.
State the next contact or handover.

spans.value: Sara begins with a clear statement:

no.value: Jeg er syk og kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

en.value: I’m ill and can’t come to work today.

spans.value: The central expression is:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb.

en.value: I can’t come to work.

spans.value: In Norwegian, på jobb means at work or to work in expressions such as være på jobb and komme på jobb.

no.value: Jeg er på jobb nå.

en.value: I’m at work now.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i morgen.

en.value: I can’t come to work tomorrow.

spans.value: You can give a brief reason if it is relevant, but you do not need to give personal details.

no.value: Jeg er dessverre syk og kan ikke komme på jobb.

en.value: Unfortunately, I’m ill and can’t come to work.

no.value: Jeg må være hjemme og kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

en.value: I have to stay home and can’t come to work today.

no.value: Jeg kan dessverre ikke møte på jobb i dag.

en.value: Unfortunately, I can’t report for work today.

spans.value: Kan ikke is direct and practical. Dessverre softens the message and is common in professional communication.
Compare:

no.value: Jeg kommer ikke på jobb i dag.

en.value: I’m not coming to work today.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

en.value: I can’t come to work today.

spans.value: The first sentence reports what will happen. The second also communicates that attending is not possible. In an absence message, kan ikke komme is often clearer.
Checkpoint: Identify the central message

Read Sara’s first turn again and locate the words that state the absence and the words that state the timing. This belongs here because the employer must understand those two facts immediately. Use the context of Sara’s Tuesday morning call. A successful response would correctly distinguish cannot come to work from today, without depending on the later details about the meeting.
A message such as Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb is incomplete if the listener does not know when the absence applies. Add the most precise timing you currently know.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

en.value: I can’t come to work today.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i morgen.

en.value: I can’t come to work tomorrow.

no.value: Jeg blir borte hele dagen.

en.value: I’ll be away all day.

no.value: Jeg blir hjemme i dag og i morgen.

en.value: I’ll stay home today and tomorrow.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme før etter lunsj.

en.value: I can’t come in until after lunch.

spans.value: The Norwegian structure før etter lunsj is possible in conversation, but the clearer workplace message is:

no.value: Jeg kan komme på jobb etter lunsj, men ikke før.

en.value: I can come to work after lunch, but not before.

spans.value: If you are uncertain about the following day, state only what you know and promise an update.

no.value: Jeg blir hjemme i dag. Jeg vet ikke ennå om jeg kan komme i morgen.

en.value: I’ll stay home today. I don’t know yet whether I can come tomorrow.

no.value: Jeg gir deg beskjed senere i dag.

en.value: I’ll let you know later today.

spans.value: This is better than making a promise you may not be able to keep.
Common mistake: vague timing
A message can be grammatically correct but still unhelpful:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb.

en.value: I can’t come to work.

spans.value: The employer may have to ask whether you mean this morning, the whole day, or several days. Add timing:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i dag. Jeg blir borte hele dagen.

en.value: I can’t come to work today. I’ll be away all day.

spans.value: Checkpoint: Make the timing precise

Imagine that Sara knows she will be absent for all of Tuesday but does not yet know about Wednesday. Draft the timing part of her message without adding new personal details. This activity belongs here because it separates confirmed information from uncertain information. A successful response would state Tuesday’s full-day absence clearly and leave Wednesday open for a later update.
After reporting the absence, tell the other person when they will hear from you again. Useful expressions include:

no.value: Jeg gir deg beskjed i ettermiddag.

en.value: I’ll let you know this afternoon.

no.value: Jeg kontakter deg senere i dag.

en.value: I’ll contact you later today.

no.value: Jeg sender en oppdatering innen klokka tre.

en.value: I’ll send an update by three o’clock.

no.value: Jeg ringer deg i morgen tidlig.

en.value: I’ll call you tomorrow morning.

spans.value: The expression gi beskjed means to let someone know or give someone a message. You normally include the person as an object when necessary:

no.value: Jeg gir Henrik beskjed i ettermiddag.

en.value: I’ll let Henrik know this afternoon.

spans.value: When the listener is already clear, you can use deg:

no.value: Jeg gir deg beskjed innen klokka tre.

en.value: I’ll let you know by three o’clock.

spans.value: Notice the difference between a general time and a deadline:

no.value: Jeg sender en oppdatering klokka tre.

en.value: I’ll send an update at three o’clock.

no.value: Jeg sender en oppdatering innen klokka tre.

en.value: I’ll send an update by three o’clock.

spans.value: Klokka tre names the expected time. Innen klokka tre means no later than three.
Checkpoint: Add the next contact

Return to Sara’s situation. Her team leader needs to know whether she can work on Wednesday. Add one sentence promising an update by a specific time on Tuesday. This belongs after the timing statement because it tells Henrik how the remaining uncertainty will be resolved. A successful response would name both the contact action and its deadline.
Sometimes another person must handle an urgent task while you are away. A short handover statement prevents confusion.

no.value: Nora kan ta kundemøtet.

en.value: Nora can take the customer meeting.

no.value: Jeg har sendt notatene til Nora.

en.value: I’ve sent the notes to Nora.

no.value: Per følger opp kunden i dag.

en.value: Per will follow up with the customer today.

no.value: Dokumentene ligger i prosjektmappen.

en.value: The documents are in the project folder.

spans.value: A strong handover often names the task and the person:

no.value: Nora kan ta møtet klokka ti.

en.value: Nora can take the meeting at ten.

spans.value: It can also say where the necessary information is:

no.value: Jeg har sendt henne notatene.

en.value: I’ve sent her the notes.

no.value: Planen ligger i fellesmappen.

en.value: The plan is in the shared folder.

spans.value: Keep the handover limited to information the employer needs immediately. Sara does not explain the whole customer case during her absence call. She states who can take the meeting and confirms that the notes have been sent.
Common mistake: mentioning a task without resolving it
This statement identifies a problem but not a handover:

no.value: Jeg har et kundemøte klokka ti.

en.value: I have a customer meeting at ten.

spans.value: A more useful message states what will happen:

no.value: Jeg har et kundemøte klokka ti, men Nora kan ta det.

en.value: I have a customer meeting at ten, but Nora can take it.

spans.value: The pronoun det refers to møtet.
Checkpoint: Complete the handover

Imagine that Sara cannot lead the ten o’clock meeting. Write a short handover statement saying that Nora can take it and that Nora has received the notes. This activity belongs here because Sara’s absence affects a specific scheduled task. A successful response would identify the replacement and confirm that the necessary material has been transferred.
A complete message does not need to be long:

no.value: Hei, Henrik. Jeg er dessverre syk og kan ikke komme på jobb i dag. Jeg blir hjemme hele dagen. Nora kan ta kundemøtet, og jeg har sendt henne notatene. Jeg gir deg beskjed innen klokka tre om jeg kan komme på jobb i morgen.

en.value: Hi, Henrik. Unfortunately, I’m ill and can’t come to work today. I’ll stay home all day. Nora can take the customer meeting, and I’ve sent her the notes. I’ll let you know by three o’clock whether I can come to work tomorrow.

spans.value: The order helps the reader:

items.value: The handover deals with urgent work.
The next contact closes the message.

spans.value: Avoid hiding the main point behind a long introduction. Henrik should not have to read several sentences before discovering that Sara will be absent.

sections.title: Common mistakes in a complete message

spans.value: Do not confuse i dag and på dagen:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

en.value: I can’t come to work today.

spans.value: I dag gives the correct timing. På dagen usually means during the daytime and does not identify the date by itself.
Do not omit på in komme på jobb:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme jobb i dag.

en.value: I can’t come work today.

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.

en.value: I can’t come to work today.

spans.value: Do not promise a future contact without saying when if the timing matters:

no.value: Jeg sier fra senere.

en.value: I’ll let you know later.

spans.value: Clearer:

no.value: Jeg gir deg beskjed innen klokka tre.

en.value: I’ll let you know by three o’clock.

sections.title: Practice: Build a message in stages

spans.value: Imagine that Emil works in a warehouse. On Thursday morning, he cannot attend his shift. He knows he will be absent for the whole day. A colleague, Lise, can receive an expected delivery, and Emil will contact his manager by four about Friday.

First, write only Emil’s central absence statement and Thursday timing. This controlled step belongs here because it tests whether the main message remains clear before other information is added. A successful response would state that Emil cannot come to work on Thursday and will be away all day.
At 2:40, Sara sends Henrik an update.
Hei igjen. Jeg er fortsatt syk, så jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i morgen heller. Jeg kontakter deg i morgen ettermiddag om torsdag.

blocks.translation: Hi again. I’m still ill, so I can’t come to work tomorrow either. I’ll contact you tomorrow afternoon about Thursday.

spans.value: Takk for oppdateringen. Nora tok kundemøtet, og det gikk bra. God bedring videre.

blocks.translation: Thanks for the update. Nora took the customer meeting, and it went well. Get well soon.

spans.value: Sara follows the plan from the morning call: she contacts Henrik before three, gives the new timing, and states when the next update will come. Her second message is brief because the background and handover are already known.

Without looking back at Sara’s messages, write a short workplace absence message for a new situation. State that you cannot attend work, give clear timing, and finish with either a specific next contact or a practical handover. A successful response will let the employer understand what is happening, when it applies, and what will happen next.

prompt.value: Sara says: «Hei, Henrik. Det er Sara. Jeg er dessverre syk og kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.» Choose the option that identifies both the absence and its timing, without using later meeting details.

options.text: Jeg er syk og kan ikke komme på jobb i dag.
options.why: This identifies both the absence and the fact that it applies today.

options.text: Jeg kan ikke komme på jobb i morgen.
options.why: This gives tomorrow as the timing, not today.
This says that the speaker is at work, not absent.

options.text: Jeg kan komme på jobb etter lunsj, men ikke før.
options.why: This describes coming after lunch rather than being unable to come today.

stem.value: Which option states both Sara's absence and its timing?

prompt.value: Build the complete Norwegian timing message. Say that Sara stays home today (Tuesday) and does not yet know whether she can come tomorrow (Wednesday). Use every token exactly once.
Build one Norwegian sentence for Sara to say to her team leader on Tuesday. Promise an update by a specific time.
Build one short Norwegian handover sentence. State that Nora can take the ten o'clock meeting and that you have sent her the notes.
Build one Norwegian absence statement for Emil. Say that he cannot come to work on Thursday and will be away all day.
Build one Norwegian handover sentence saying that Lise can receive the delivery.
Write a concise professional Norwegian message for Emil. State that he cannot come to work on Thursday, will be away all day, and will update his manager by four about whether he can work on Friday.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept equivalent natural Bokmål wording and either one sentence or several short sentences, provided all requested facts remain clear.

criteria.instruction: States that Emil cannot come to work on Thursday.
States that Emil will be away all day.
States that Emil will update his manager by four about whether he can work on Friday.

prompt.value: Imagine you work at a library and cannot attend your Friday shift. Write a short Norwegian workplace absence message for this new situation. Use original wording. State that you cannot come to work, give clear timing, and finish with either a specific next contact or a practical handover.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept equivalent natural Bokmål wording and either a concrete next contact or a concrete handover. Do not require exact lesson wording.

criteria.instruction: Uses the new library and Friday-shift situation without copying a complete lesson sentence.
States that the writer cannot attend work.
Gives clear timing for the absence.
Finishes with either a specific next contact or a practical handover.
